reviews.title: A Cute Little Monitor & USB Hub!
reviews.comment: The monitor is really small in size, and the build quality feels average—not top-quality, but not cheap either. In terms of functionality, it works exactly as you would expect from this type of product. Personally, I use it to monitor my PC’s performance, but it can also be used as a regular monitor. The color range is good, and so far everything has been working well; I haven’t had any issues. As for the price, it’s true that it’s a bit expensive if you look at it strictly as a 3.5” monitor; however, it also works as a hub, which adds more value. Even so, I still feel it’s a bit pricey for what it offers. That said, if price isn’t a problem for you and you want something cute, small, that doesn’t take up any space, and is fully functional visually, this one works without any problems. I really like the design—it fits perfectly with the little retro build I’m putting together, so I have no complaints about that.
reviews.author: SnowRa

reviews.title: A cute little hub that is a great display, although it could be better.
reviews.comment: This hub is rather pricey for what it is, but you're buying this for the screen. The actual screen part of it is nice, it is obviously small but it works great for some games or videos. It's relatively clear and it gets plenty bright. The actual hub itself works great, having no issues with any cables or storage devices I plug into it. Setup was easy too, just had to plug in my HDMI cable and USB-C cable. The device itself feels fine, although the stand is a little cheap feeling and moves easily. It'd be nice if it had rubber feet on the bottom. My biggest complaint is the lack of auto shutoff. Anytime you turn your computer off, it will show a "NO SIGNAL" box in the middle of the screen that doesn't go away. It will not turn itself off and will likely suffer burn in issues if you don't make sure to turn it off every time you shut your computer off. Past that issue, it works great for what I wanted and I can recommend it as a novel USB hub.
reviews.author: Corey Rutter

reviews.title: Hagabis mini monitor - usb hub.. awesome!
reviews.comment: I've wanted one of these things for a long while and I finally got one! It sits like a small computer on my desk and with the help of some speakers and a firestick I'm able to watch tv as I use my computer! I really like this thing because almost everything on it works. Except I've been unable to get a full sized sd card into the sd slot. Micro-sd's work just fine.. now, the only thing that drives me crazy about the thing is the chinese like to turn things upside down.. like the usb slots and if I'm not mistaken the hdmi slot as well.. why? why? why? but I've gotten used to it. Comes with a well made cable for power and hooked up to your computer you can use it as a second monitor. I like that but one day everything was flipped and I didn't know how to flip it back.. meaning my computer screen was on the hagabis screen and I couldn't really see anything well to use my computer. That was a bit frustrating but it's back to normal and I figured out just using a firestick was a lot easier than hooking it directly to my computer. Of all of my things. this has got to be one of my favorites! and I'm honestly glad I bought it! It's designed really well..  weighs next to nothing.. and speaking it costs a little over $100 but for a 100,000 hours before failure rate.. that's really not bad! It has two buttons.. one for changing brightness, and the other turns on and off the monitor. Easy to set up by just plugging it in more or less.. I'd recommend this to anyone seeking a good monitor that they can use to watch tv, movies, or use as a spare monitor. Now keep in mind it doesn't have built in speakers so you'll need some to listen to what you want to watch. I hope this helps you to understand what you're buying and I think this truly is.. a good buy!!
reviews.author: Brent Price

reviews.title: Tiny Beige Box PC
reviews.comment: Cute lil' thing.  Does what it claims. For those who are wondering, yes, there is enough room to squeeze a Raspberry Pi in there; but probably not the way you are thinking. The connector for the display is similar to DSI but not quite, and the ribbon cables are epoxied in place so they are very hard to get apart without damage and probably impossible to make work with the Pi. Instead of fighting all that I ordered a 3.2" touchscreen to plug into the gpio header of a Pi Zero 2, which will live behind it in the monitor part of the model PC.  I'll hook up the interface board in the bottom (if it still works after fighting to get it apart) and should end up with a really cool micro PC, with about the power of a top-spec Pentium system of the beige box era with the hottest graphics board and biggest hard drive array imaginable at the time.  Seems appropriate. You could probably also just barely squeeze a full size Raspberry Pi in the bottom section and fit an HDMI monitor up top, but you would have to cut holes for all the ports, but it would be such a tight fit it would probably run hot, and there would be no really good way to mount the board.  Not worth the hassle IMHO. Manufacturer: if you are reading this, you should totally make a version for the Raspberry Pi 5!  You'll sell the heck out of them.
reviews.author: Alaskan Flyer

reviews.title: CANNOT RETURN
reviews.comment: NOT EASY TO SET UP! No my friend, this is not a plug-and-play like you see. You have to download its software. Then you have to go find the download documents on your computer and apply it to the screen, and set up the coding. Absolutely trash! I was expecting a easy plug and Play so I could keep like my discord on the side or something. But no. It was an aggravating 2 hours of having to figure everything out. The instructions don't even mention it, all the instructions mentioned, are how to plug it in. The rest you have to scan the link on your phone, and then get that link to pop up on your computer to do the rest. It is highly aggravating. And if I hadn't spent $100, I would have checked it over a bridge. Knowing this now, there's no way I would have bought this for $100. This thing is worth $10 at most, if it can set up, then I guess you could price it around there. But no, this is like getting a car in the mail that you have to put together. Also, there is no return. This is definitely a scam. I don't know how Amazon is allowing this.
reviews.author: Clay
